# Paw Proxy (paw-proxy)

> Zero-config HTTPS proxy for local macOS development. Provides automatic HTTPS for .test domains with trusted certificates, DNS resolution, and reverse proxying — no per-project configuration needed.

paw-proxy eliminates the friction of local HTTPS development. It runs a daemon that handles DNS resolution (`*.test` → `127.0.0.1`), generates trusted TLS certificates on demand, and reverse-proxies HTTPS traffic to your dev server's local port.

Two binaries: `paw-proxy` (daemon and management CLI) and `up` (dev server wrapper), shipped inside Paw Proxy.app, a macOS menu bar app that runs the daemon as its background item and shows your routes. Run `up bun dev` and your app is available at `https://myapp.test`.

Requirements: macOS 13 or later, Apple silicon. Distributed as a Homebrew cask.

Key features:
- Automatic .test TLD DNS resolution (local DNS server on port 9353)
- On-demand HTTPS certificate generation (ECDSA P-256, signed by local CA)
- WebSocket support with raw TCP proxying
- Unix socket API for route management
- Daemon runs as Paw Proxy.app's background item (SMAppService agent `com.alexcatdad.paw-proxy.daemon`)
- Docker Compose mode: `up docker compose up` registers `service.project.test` for each service with a published port
- Worktree-friendly: a name already in use from another directory falls back to the directory name
- Smart naming from package.json or directory name
- Auto-restart on crash with `--restart` flag
- Menu bar app: status header, setup/background item/daemon rows, route list (click to open), status badge on the tray icon, opt-in "project is live" notifications
- No telemetry, analytics or network update checks

## Installation

### Via Homebrew (Recommended)

```
brew install --cask alexcatdad/tap/paw-proxy
sudo paw-proxy setup
```

The cask installs Paw Proxy.app and links its bundled `paw-proxy` and `up` helpers onto your PATH. Upgrade with `brew upgrade --cask paw-proxy`; the menu bar panel offers "Restart to finish update" until the daemon runs the new version (or run `paw-proxy restart`).

### From Source

Bare binaries are for development. On macOS, setup expects `paw-proxy` inside Paw Proxy.app and refuses to write the legacy LaunchAgent unless you pass `--legacy-launchagent`. See CONTRIBUTING.md for building the app (`task macos:dev`).

### What Setup Does

1. Creates support directory: `~/Library/Application Support/paw-proxy` (mode 0700)
2. Generates CA certificate: RSA 4096-bit, 10-year validity, saved as `ca.crt` and `ca.key` (mode 0600)
3. Trusts CA in macOS keychain (login keychain, falls back to System keychain)
4. Creates DNS resolver: `/etc/resolver/test` pointing to `127.0.0.1:9353`
5. Hands the daemon to Paw Proxy.app, which registers it as a background item (macOS may show "Background Items Added", or ask you to allow it in System Settings › General › Login Items)

Restart your browser afterwards so it picks up the new CA.

### Uninstall

```
sudo paw-proxy uninstall
```

Removes CA from keychain, deletes resolver, stops and removes the daemon, deletes support directory. Then `brew uninstall --cask paw-proxy` removes the app.

## Usage

### Basic Workflow

```
cd ~/projects/myapp
up bun dev
```

Output:
```
🔗 Mapping https://myapp.test -> localhost:3847...
🚀 Project is live at: https://myapp.test
------------------------------------------------
```

What happens:
1. `up` connects to the daemon's unix socket and verifies it's running
2. Determines app name from `-n` flag, `package.json` name, or directory name
3. Finds a free port on 127.0.0.1
4. Registers route with daemon: `myapp` → `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`
5. Sets environment variables and runs `bun dev`
6. Sends heartbeat every 10 seconds to keep route alive
7. On exit (Ctrl+C), deregisters route from daemon

### Custom Domain Name

```
up -n api bun dev
# App available at https://api.test
```

### Auto-Restart on Crash

```
up --restart bun dev
# Restarts automatically on non-zero exit, 1s delay between restarts
```

### Environment Variables

`up` sets these for the child process:

| Variable | Example | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| PORT | 3847 | Port your dev server should bind to |
| APP_DOMAIN | myapp.test | Domain name |
| APP_URL | https://myapp.test | Full HTTPS URL |
| HTTPS | true | Indicates HTTPS is available |
| NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS | ~/Library/Application Support/paw-proxy/ca.crt | CA cert path for Node.js |

### Route Name Resolution

1. If `-n name` flag is provided, use that (sanitized)
2. Else if `package.json` exists in current directory, use its `name` field (sanitized)
3. Else use directory name (sanitized)

Sanitization: lowercase, replace non-alphanumeric with `-`, trim leading/trailing `-`, prepend `app-` if starts with digit, max 63 chars.

If the name is already registered from a different directory (e.g. a git worktree of the same project), `up` falls back to the directory name and prints a warning.

### Docker Compose

```
up docker compose up
# Mapping https://frontend.myapp.test -> localhost:3000...
# Mapping https://api.myapp.test -> localhost:8080...
```

Every service with a published port gets `<service>.<project>.test`; services without published ports are skipped. `-n` overrides the project name; compose flags (`--profile`, `-f`) pass through.

## Menu Bar App

Paw Proxy.app lives in the menu bar (paw icon; a badge appears when setup, approval, the daemon or an update needs attention). The panel shows:
- A status header: "Running — N routes", or what needs doing ("Setup needed", "Waiting for approval", "Proxy not responding", "Restart to finish update") with one primary action button
- Rows for Setup (CA and DNS), Background item (macOS approval) and Daemon (version and uptime)
- Routes: each name with upstream port, project folder and last heartbeat; stale routes are dimmed; click to open, right-click to copy the URL
- Restart proxy, Open logs, Turn proxy off, Settings, Quit (the proxy keeps running after you quit)

Settings: "Notify me when projects go live" (off by default; macOS asks for permission when turned on), "Play a sound" (notifications are silent otherwise), "Launch at login". Notifications are posted by the app bundle; `up` reports route events to the daemon (`POST /notifications`) and the app polls them (`GET /notifications`). Clicking a notification opens the project's URL.

## CLI Commands

### paw-proxy setup

```
sudo paw-proxy setup
```

Performs complete setup: CA generation, keychain trust, DNS resolver, daemon registration through Paw Proxy.app. Idempotent — safe to re-run. Requires sudo for `/etc/resolver` and keychain modifications.

### paw-proxy uninstall

```
sudo paw-proxy uninstall [--brew]
```

Removes all paw-proxy components. The `--brew` flag skips the interactive CA removal prompt.

### paw-proxy restart

```
paw-proxy restart
```

Restarts the daemon, e.g. to pick up an upgraded binary.

### paw-proxy status

```
paw-proxy status
```

Shows daemon status, uptime, version, active routes with upstreams, and CA expiration date.

Example output:
```
Status: ✅ Running (v1.2.0, up 2h15m)

Routes:
  • myapp.test -> localhost:3847 (45m30s)
    Dir: /Users/alex/projects/myapp
  • api.test -> localhost:4200 (12m15s)
    Dir: /Users/alex/projects/api

CA Expires: 2036-02-10
```

### paw-proxy run

```
paw-proxy run
```

Starts the daemon in foreground. Normally launched by the app's background item, not run manually. Starts 5 goroutines: DNS server (port 9353), API server (unix socket), HTTP server (port 80, redirects to HTTPS), HTTPS server (port 443), and cleanup routine (evicts stale routes every 10s).

### paw-proxy logs

```
paw-proxy logs [--tail|-f] [--clear]
```

- No flags: shows last 50 lines from `~/Library/Logs/paw-proxy.log`
- `--tail` or `-f`: follows log output in real time (like `tail -f`)
- `--clear`: truncates the log file

### paw-proxy doctor

```
paw-proxy doctor
```

Checks the unix socket, daemon health, the `/etc/resolver/test` file, the DNS server's A and AAAA answers, system DNS resolution of a `.test` name, and the HTTPS TLS handshake on every advertised and system-resolved address, independently of whether any dev server is running.

### paw-proxy version

```
paw-proxy version
```

Prints version string (injected at build time via ldflags).

## Architecture

### Component Overview

```
┌─────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
│   Browser   │────▶│  paw-proxy   │────▶│  Dev Server  │
│             │     │  (port 443)  │     │  (dynamic)   │
└─────────────┘     └──────────────┘     └──────────────┘
                           │
                    ┌──────┴──────┐
                    │  DNS Server  │
                    │  (port 9353) │
                    └──────────────┘
```

### Request Flow

1. Browser queries DNS for `myapp.test`
2. macOS reads `/etc/resolver/test`, forwards to `127.0.0.1:9353`
3. paw-proxy DNS server responds: A record → 127.0.0.1, AAAA → NOERROR with no answers (IPv4-only listeners)
4. Browser connects to `127.0.0.1:443`
5. TLS handshake: daemon generates ECDSA P-256 cert for `myapp.test`, signed by CA, cached in LRU cache (max 1000 entries)
6. Daemon extracts Host header, strips `.test` suffix, looks up route in registry
7. Proxy forwards request to upstream with X-Forwarded-For/Proto/Host headers
8. For WebSocket: hijacks connection, runs bidirectional `io.Copy`

### Project Structure

```
internal/
├── api/        # Unix socket API and route registry
│   ├── server.go     # HTTP handlers, input validation, rate limiting
│   └── routes.go     # RouteRegistry with RWMutex, CRUD, cleanup
├── daemon/     # Main daemon orchestrator
│   └── daemon.go     # Launches goroutines, TLS config, graceful shutdown
├── dns/        # DNS server for .test TLD
│   └── server.go     # UDP-only, A responses and AAAA NODATA for *.test
├── proxy/      # Reverse proxy with WebSocket support
│   └── proxy.go      # HTTP forwarding + raw TCP WebSocket proxy
├── setup/      # macOS setup/uninstall (darwin-only)
│   ├── setup_darwin.go    # CA, keychain, resolver, daemon hand-off to the app
│   ├── setup_other.go     # Stub for non-macOS
│   └── uninstall_darwin.go
└── ssl/        # CA generation + per-domain cert cache
    ├── ca.go         # RSA 4096-bit CA, 10-year validity
    └── cert.go       # ECDSA P-256 leaf certs, LRU cache (max 1000)

cmd/
├── paw-proxy/  # Main CLI entry point
│   └── main.go
├── up/         # Dev server wrapper entry point
│   └── main.go
└── gen-man/    # Man page generator
    └── main.go

macos/          # Paw Proxy.app (Swift package, MenubarKit)
```

### Security Model

**SSRF Prevention:** Upstream URLs validated to localhost only — `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`. Prevents proxying to external or internal network hosts.

**Route Name Validation:** Regex `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{0,62}$` (dots allow Compose names like `api.myapp`).

**Directory Validation:** Must be absolute path (starts with `/`), no path traversal (`..` components rejected).

**Certificate Trust Chain:** CA cert (RSA 4096-bit, self-signed) → leaf cert (ECDSA P-256, 1-year validity). CA trusted in macOS keychain.

**File Permissions:** Support directory 0700, CA private key 0600, unix socket 0600.

**TLS Configuration:** TLS 1.2 minimum. Cipher suites: ECDHE with AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305.

**Network Binding:** HTTP and HTTPS servers bind to `127.0.0.1` (loopback only).

**Privacy:** No telemetry, analytics or update checks over the network. The CA private key is never logged or exported. Only setup and uninstall need sudo.

## Unix Socket API

The daemon exposes a control API via unix socket at `~/Library/Application Support/paw-proxy/paw-proxy.sock`.

### POST /routes

Register a new route.

Request:
```json
{"name": "myapp", "upstream": "http://127.0.0.1:3000", "dir": "/Users/alex/projects/myapp"}
```

Validation:
- `name`: matches `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{0,62}$`
- `upstream`: must be localhost (127.0.0.1, ::1, or localhost)
- `dir`: must be absolute path, no traversal

Response 200:
```json
{"status": "registered"}
```

Response 409 (conflict):
```json
{"error": "route already exists", "existingDir": "/Users/alex/other-project"}
```

### DELETE /routes/{name}

Deregister a route.

Response 200: `{"status": "deregistered"}`
Response 404: `{"error": "route not found"}`

### POST /routes/{name}/heartbeat

Keep route alive. Routes expire after 30 seconds without a heartbeat.

Response 200: `{"status": "ok"}`
Response 404: `{"error": "route not found"}`

### GET /routes

List all registered routes.

Response 200:
```json
[{"name": "myapp", "upstream": "http://127.0.0.1:3000", "dir": "/Users/alex/projects/myapp", "registered": "2026-02-12T10:30:00Z", "lastHeartbeat": "2026-02-12T10:30:45Z"}]
```

### GET /health

Health check.

Response 200:
```json
{"status": "ok", "version": "1.2.0", "uptime": "2h15m30s"}
```

### POST /notifications and GET /notifications?after=<cursor>

`up` reports route events (project live / stopped) with POST; the menu bar app reads them with GET, which also returns a per-boot `epoch`. The cursor is only valid within one epoch.

### Curl Examples

```
# Health check
curl --unix-socket ~/Library/Application\ Support/paw-proxy/paw-proxy.sock http://unix/health

# List routes
curl --unix-socket ~/Library/Application\ Support/paw-proxy/paw-proxy.sock http://unix/routes

# Register route
curl --unix-socket ~/Library/Application\ Support/paw-proxy/paw-proxy.sock \
  -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"myapp","upstream":"http://127.0.0.1:3000","dir":"/tmp/myapp"}' \
  http://unix/routes

# Deregister route
curl --unix-socket ~/Library/Application\ Support/paw-proxy/paw-proxy.sock \
  -X DELETE http://unix/routes/myapp
```

## Troubleshooting

### Quick Diagnostics

```
paw-proxy doctor    # DNS, socket, daemon and TLS checks
paw-proxy status    # Daemon status and routes
paw-proxy logs -f   # Follow daemon logs
```

### Setup Fails with Permission Error

Cause: Setup modifies `/etc/resolver` and the keychain.
Fix: Run with sudo: `sudo paw-proxy setup`

### Certificate Not Trusted in Browser

Cause: CA not in keychain or not trusted.
Diagnose:
```
security find-certificate -c "paw-proxy CA" ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db
```
Fix: Re-run `sudo paw-proxy setup` to re-trust the CA.

### Firefox Doesn't Trust Certificate

Cause: Firefox uses its own certificate store, not the macOS keychain.
Fix: Install NSS tools and re-run setup:
```
brew install nss
sudo paw-proxy setup
```

### "Daemon Not Running" Error

Cause: The background item is off, waiting for approval, or the daemon crashed. The menu bar panel names which.
Diagnose:
```
paw-proxy status
paw-proxy logs
```
Fix: Use the panel's action (Turn On Proxy, Open Login Items, Restart Proxy), run `paw-proxy restart`, or re-run `sudo paw-proxy setup`.

### Port 80 or 443 Already in Use

Cause: Another web server (nginx, Apache, etc.) is using the port.
Diagnose:
```
lsof -i :443
lsof -i :80
```
Fix: Stop the conflicting service before running setup.

### DNS Resolution Fails

Cause: Resolver file missing or daemon DNS server not running.
Diagnose:
```
cat /etc/resolver/test
# Should contain: nameserver 127.0.0.1 and port 9353
dig myapp.test @127.0.0.1 -p 9353
```
Fix: Re-run `sudo paw-proxy setup` to recreate resolver file.

### Route Disappears After ~30 Seconds

Cause: The `up` process died or heartbeat is failing.
Diagnose: Check if `up` is running: `ps aux | grep up`
Fix: Restart `up` or check daemon logs for heartbeat errors.

### Route Name Conflict

Cause: Another `up` instance registered the same name from a different directory.
Behaviour: `up` falls back to the directory name (e.g. `myapp-feat-auth.test`). Use `-n` to pick a name yourself: `up -n myapp2 bun dev`

### WebSocket Closes After an Hour Idle

Cause: WebSocket connections close after 1 hour with no data in either direction (idle timeout).
Fix: Reconnect from the client, or send periodic pings.

### Long Streaming Responses Are Cut After 2 Minutes

Cause: The HTTPS server has a 2-minute write timeout per response, which also applies to server-sent events.
Fix: Let the client reconnect (EventSource does this automatically).

### NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS Not Working

Cause: Node.js was started outside of `up`, so the env var wasn't set.
Fix: Always start Node.js via `up`: `up node server.js`

## Development

### Prerequisites

- Go 1.27.4 (matches go.mod), Swift 6 / Xcode for the app, Task
- macOS for integration tests
- Single external Go dependency: `github.com/miekg/dns`

### Build and Test

```
# Full local gate (what CI runs)
task check

# Build
go build -o paw-proxy ./cmd/paw-proxy
go build -o up ./cmd/up

# Unit tests with race detector
go test -v -race ./...

# Vet
go vet ./...

# Lint (if golangci-lint installed)
golangci-lint run

# Integration tests (macOS, requires setup)
sudo ./paw-proxy setup
./integration-tests.sh

# Coverage
go test -cover ./...

# Regenerate man pages
go run ./cmd/gen-man
```

### Coding Conventions

- Error wrapping: `fmt.Errorf("context: %w", err)`
- Security comments: `// SECURITY: explanation`
- Build tags: `//go:build darwin` with `_other.go` stubs
- No `log.Fatal` in library code (only in `cmd/`)
- No holding locks during I/O or crypto operations
- Validate all user input at API boundary

## Files

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `~/Library/Application Support/paw-proxy/` | Support directory |
| `~/Library/Application Support/paw-proxy/ca.crt` | CA certificate |
| `~/Library/Application Support/paw-proxy/ca.key` | CA private key (mode 0600) |
| `~/Library/Application Support/paw-proxy/paw-proxy.sock` | Unix socket (mode 0600) |
| `~/Library/Logs/paw-proxy.log` | Daemon log file |
| `/etc/resolver/test` | macOS DNS resolver for .test TLD |
| `Paw Proxy.app/Contents/Library/LaunchAgents/com.alexcatdad.paw-proxy.daemon.plist` | Daemon background item (registered by the app) |
